designs.notes: Variants. Unless a requirement says otherwise, "the default build" is RATE_MATCH = 0 (the board-proven 97C receive path) and "the rate-matched build" is rm_gp (RATE_MATCH = 1, RM_OWN = 1). Board evidence is one KR260 on a short optical loopback; nothing has run against a network card. Briefs 112 (UVM bench) and 115 (SVA and formal proofs) are not merged: their items are hooks with no evidence, shown as not run.

requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.
requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model

requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.
requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions

requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.
requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors

requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.
requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart

requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.
requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path

requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.
requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame

requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)
requirements.text: With a receive clock offset of +-100 ppm and +-300 ppm from the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. A loopback has no offset, so this needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset

requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.
requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card

requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.
requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned

requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.
requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails

requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.
requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed

requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.
requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions

requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.
requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing

requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.
requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly

requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.
requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents

requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.
requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does

requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.
requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs

requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.
requirements.title: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words

requirements.text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.
requirements.title: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function adder (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/adder/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a bit-serial chain of full adders) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (16 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (ripple: 0; carry_select: 0; pipelined: STAGES), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/adder/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

designs.notes: Arithmetic library, function multiplier (brief 139a). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: arith/multiplier/model.py gives, for every input, the result that spec.md defines. It agrees with an independent formulation (a shift-and-add formulation (and, for the Booth recoding, the digit-sum identity)) on every input at small widths and with Python's integer arithmetic on random large-width inputs, and the conventions that a user could guess wrong (spec.md, last section) are pinned by examples.
requirements.title: The bit-exact model is right

requirements.text: At every parameter point listed in spec.yaml (24 exhaustive points, 14 random ones, across 3 variants), each variant's outputs equal the model's in every clock: every input is driven at the small points; edge values, runs of ones, and random inputs at the large ones. The function is exact, so there is no error bound.
requirements.title: Every variant is bit-exact against the model

requirements.text: Each variant's latency in clocks is the expression in spec.yaml (dsp: STAGES; lut_array: REG; booth_r4: REG), and the bench, run with a latency two clocks off, fails for every variant, so the passing runs prove the latency rather than assume it.
requirements.title: Latency is as specified and the bench would notice if it were not

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end checks the variants against each other and a plain reference (a single `+` or `*`, or the specification written as RTL). The jobs in formal/jobs.yaml name the widths; a proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths listed there, a bounded check holds only to its stated depth. Widths beyond the listed ones are covered by simulation, not by proof.
requirements.title: The variants are equivalent to a plain reference, by proof where the tools allow

requirements.text: Every one of the mutants in verif/mutants.yaml (one exact text change each, in the variant's RTL: an inverted condition, a wrong constant, a dropped connection, a lost reset) makes the cocotb bench fail; mutants that survive or do not build are reported, never hidden.
requirements.title: The bench catches seeded faults

requirements.text: arith/multiplier/harness holds the model, the cocotb bench, a SystemVerilog checker, coverage targets and a runner that needs nothing else from the repository. Run standalone against every variant (one small exhaustive point and one large random point each, with the checker beside the instance) it passes and the random runs meet every coverage target; run against a planted fault it fails, with and without the checker. Its generated files are the repository's own bench, so they cannot drift.
requirements.title: The packaged verification harness is a standalone deliverable that works

requirements.text: spec.yaml states an interface contract (protocol, throughput, latency, reset, clock, stalls) and integration guidance (port timing, constraints to carry). Every variant passes Verilator -Wall at every point of spec.yaml; its ports and default parameters are the ones spec.yaml states; its header states the intended primitive use before any Vivado run; spec.md is the rendering of spec.yaml; the out-of-context wrapper and the build.yaml for each variant (Artix-7 xc7a100t and K26 xck26, prepared and not run) are current and lint-clean at every point they list, so a Vivado run can start from the repository alone.

designs.notes: Variants. Unless a requirement says otherwise, "the default build" is RATE_MATCH = 0 (the board-proven 97C receive path) and "the rate-matched build" is rm_gp (RATE_MATCH = 1, RM_OWN = 1). Board evidence is one KR260 on a short optical loopback; nothing has run against a network card. Briefs 112 (UVM bench) and 115 (SVA and formal proofs) are not merged: their items are hooks with no evidence, shown as not run.

requirements.text: Scrambler, block encode and decode, gearbox and block lock produce the same bits as the bit-serial Python reference, at every bit offset, with idles, ordered sets and bit-error runs.
requirements.title: PCS encodes and decodes 64B/66B bit-exactly against an independent model

requirements.text: Frames start in lane 0 and lane 4, every terminate lane and every length residue is handled, FCS is generated and checked, and a bad FCS is counted.
requirements.title: 64-bit MAC frames correctly in both directions

requirements.text: The receive gearbox slips to the block boundary from any offset, and a run of bit errors loses lock only above the documented threshold.
requirements.title: Block lock is acquired from any bit offset and survives bit errors

requirements.text: At least 100 receive-datapath restarts on the board, each one locks and no restart corrupts a frame.
requirements.title: The link locks after every receive-datapath restart

requirements.text: With RATE_MATCH = 0 the core is equivalent to the core of main 6909e43f (brief 97C) and passes that brief's bench.
requirements.title: The default build keeps the board-proven receive path

requirements.text: The elastic buffer inserts and deletes idles only between frames, never under- or overflows silently, and every order sent is fired and passes its content check.
requirements.title: Rate matching never corrupts a frame

requirements.external: a second reference clock or a 10G network card (a loopback has no frequency offset)
requirements.text: With a receive clock offset of +-100 ppm and +-300 ppm from the transmit clock, no frame is lost or corrupted and the buffer neither overflows nor underflows. A loopback has no offset, so this needs a second reference clock or another device on the link.
requirements.title: Rate matching holds under a real frequency offset

requirements.text: The PCS and MAC exchange frames with an independent 10GBASE-R implementation. A PCS talking to itself accepts its own symmetric mistakes, so only another implementation proves the block formats and scrambler order.
requirements.title: Interoperates with a standard 10GBASE-R network card

requirements.text: Every armed decision yields exactly one order, a poisoned order never fires, and every fault counter stays 0.
requirements.title: Orders are sent only for valid decisions, none is lost or poisoned

requirements.text: A stale counter, a missing order, a counter that was not read, a wrong polarity or a link that never came up fails the run and names the cause; unsafe actions are refused without the lock.
requirements.title: The board drivers cannot report OK when a safety check fails

requirements.text: tx_disable is 1 at reset; the board run switches the laser on only after the polarity was read back.
requirements.title: The laser is off at reset and its polarity is confirmed

requirements.text: Die temperature, VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCBRAM read from SYSMON are inside the DS925 windows at the start and end of every board run.
requirements.title: Board runs stay inside the recommended operating conditions

requirements.text: report_cdc shows no Critical item and every crossing has the documented synchroniser structure.
requirements.title: No critical clock-domain crossing

requirements.text: Every address in regmap.py is decoded, nothing else is, vector widths agree, and the datasheet states unmapped reads return 0, counters read from a snapshot and reads have no side effects.
requirements.title: The register map is generated from one source and decoded exactly

requirements.text: The build files set parameters the core has, the base build keeps the 97C defaults, and each variant differs from the base only where documented.
requirements.title: Every build variant sets only the parameters it documents

requirements.text: es_ctrl aborts a point on a DRP timeout, latches the point at start, restores every DRP word and is absent when EYESCAN = 0.
requirements.title: The eye-scan sequencer drives the GT's DRP as its Python twin does

requirements.text: The write and read pointers of rate_match_gp count modulo 2^CW and cross by gray code. For every width CW > 0 and every value, the gray codes of b and b + 1 (including the wrap from 2^CW - 1 to 0) differ in exactly one bit, so a sample taken while the pointer moves is the old or the new code.
requirements.title: A pointer's gray code changes in exactly one bit per count, at every width

requirements.text: For every width and value, the decoder of the pointer crossing returns the count the encoder was given; and a sampled code that is the old or the new code decodes to the old or the new count.
requirements.title: Gray decoding inverts gray encoding, at every width

requirements.text: Brief 119's tcp_fast.sv builds the IPv4 header checksum from a precomputed template plus the changing fields. For all TTL, address and identification values it equals the complement of the ones' complement sum of the header, and the filled-in header sums to 0xFFFF.
requirements.title: The IPv4 header checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs

requirements.text: For all addresses, ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, windows and payloads of up to 30 sixteen-bit words, the checksum the RTL equations produce equals the complement of the ones' complement sum over pseudo-header, header and payload. The byte-pair swapping, the streaming receive check and the timing are not modelled.
requirements.title: The TCP checksum of the TCP fast path equals the Internet checksum, for all inputs and payloads up to 30 words

requirements.text: The ones' complement sum of any list of 16-bit words equals the natural-number sum reduced mod 65535, and RFC 1624 equation 3 (incremental update) is correct for a header of any length when the new header is not all zero words; for an all-zero header it gives 0x0000. No current RTL patches a checksum in place; this is the arithmetic the fast path's template-plus-fields form relies on.
requirements.title: The ones' complement arithmetic the checksum equations rest on is correct, for lists of any length

requirements.text: For a packed pattern e * m + f with fraction f < m (m = 2^MAN), adding the rounding increment 1 either raises the fraction by one or, when the fraction is all ones, raises the exponent by one and leaves a zero fraction: the identity fp_pack's single add on the packed {exponent, fraction} pattern rests on, so a significand overflow, a subnormal rounding up to the smallest normal number and a largest finite number rounding up to infinity need no special case. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. content.framing: The human specifies the requirements and checks that the verification is thorough enough. The agent holds the knowledge to implement and to verify. You can open any of the implementation or the evidence, and you do not have to. Hardware on the board, with attached instruments, is a verification layer of its own: where a requirement depends on something outside the design (an optical link, a network card, a data source) it may be the only way to close it.
